title: Binomial / Poisson Cumulative
summary: Single-term and range probabilities for Bin(n,p) and Po(λ). 110 bytes.

body.text: nCr types one binomial term; a CDF is a loop. This WebCal version II listing auto-detects the law: if the second input is a probability in (0,1) it is Binomial (then n, p, k); otherwise it is Poisson (λ, k). Enter an upper index at the next prompt for P(k ≤ X ≤ m). EXE through extra terms, then 0 EXE to print the sum. AC after a one-term run. nCr is SHIFT ÷. On the fx-50FH II the × after nCr may be omitted (109 bytes) and A^(B)÷B!e^(A needs no extra brackets.

body.label: Memory / run mode
body.text: 110 bytes (109 on fx-50FH II) of the shared 680-byte pool. Create the slot in COMP. Type ? → : ◢ Goto Lbl If Then from SHIFT 3 (P-CMD).

body.caption: Bin(9, 0.5). Shaded bars k = 4, 5, 6 sum to 0.65625.

body.text: Question: Use this program to solve the case: X ~ Bin(9, 0.5), P(X = 4).
Given: Second input 0.5 is in (0,1), so the third prompt is k.
Question: Use this program to solve the case: Same X, P(4 ≤ X ≤ 6).
Given: After k = 4, enter the upper index 6.

items: Or 4 【EXE】, 【EXE】, 【EXE】 to see 0.24609, 0.24609, 0.16406, then 0 【EXE】 for the sum

body.text: Example 3 (edge): X ~ Po(5), P(X = 4) and P(4 ≤ X ≤ 6)
Question: Use this program to solve the case: X ~ Po(5), P(X = 4) and P(4 ≤ X ≤ 6).
Given: Second input 4 is not a probability, so A is λ.

body.label: Pitfalls
body.text: Do not enter p = 0 or p = 1 as the second input — those look like Poisson. P(X=0) for Poisson: λ EXE 0 EXE. The running sum lives in M. Source: WebCal binomial_PoissonDist2.htm.
